subject: physics
question_text: Show that in free fall the acceleration of a body does not depend on its mass.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: The force and the law
lines: In free fall the only force is the weight:
and by Newton’s second law F = m a.
steps.why: The same m appears on both sides because the mass that feels gravity and the mass that resists acceleration are the same quantity.
common_mistakes: Including air resistance. Free fall means gravity alone.

recall.must_convey: That in free fall the only force is m g and Newton’s second law gives F equals m a.

steps.memory_tip: The same m sits on both sides. That is why it can cancel.
steps.margin_note: Write both expressions before equating them.

steps.label: The cancellation
lines: m a = m g, and m is not zero, so

lines.text: a = g, independent of the mass m

lines: A heavy body and a light body dropped
together reach the ground at the same time.
steps.why: Because m divides out, the acceleration is the same number for every body, which is why a coin and a feather fall together once air is removed.
common_mistakes: Saying heavier bodies fall faster. They feel a larger force but also resist it more, and the two effects cancel exactly.

recall.must_convey: That m cancels, so a equals g and the acceleration does not depend on the mass.

steps.memory_tip: Bigger mass means bigger pull AND bigger resistance. They cancel exactly.
steps.margin_note: Say "m is not zero" before dividing.

insider_note: The mass cancels in one line. Write that cancellation out — it is the whole answer.
